full_judgment:
8. This Court, being a Court of record. article 108 of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh has conferred upon this Court the power to make order for investigation as well as to punish for contempt of this Court. This power is inherent, indispensable and is not subject to any kind of abridgement or limitation. No law is required to be enacted or promulgated for exercising this power. Besides, conferment of this power is the fundamental pre-requisite for ensuing the rule of law as well as to find justification in establishing, maintaining and continuation of an independent judicial system in any democratic polity governed by and under the Constitution of the Republic. 

 10. The conducts in different quarters, frequently flouting the Court's orders and speaking unscrupulously in a manner that may bring the dignity of this Court down to the estimation of the people, more so when some one talking is not even aware of his limitation about the subject matter he is taking about and is posing him, as an expert or supra-Court entity, the attitude of this Court to ignore these self-proclaimed experts indulging themselves in talking about even the matter sub-judice before the Court. If a contempt proceeding is rendered to a mere procedural or a paper-formality to be ended in accepting, invariably in all cases, the apology made then perhaps one day the Court may not see compliance of its order or upholding its dignity, which is the pre- condition to ensure that the state is being governed according to law, not by the law breakers. The situation, if so arises, is bound to collapse the rule of law, which is not contemplated by the founding fathers of our Constitution (as obvious from keeping article 108). The law abiding citizens (who are the majority) of our country would be left unprotected in the hands of the mightiest, the pressure groups and vested quarters; and would also be exposed to arbitrary and unlawful treatment. This Court cannot be a helpless spectator to all these.
